Class AnchorPanelAdapter

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.panel.AnchorPanelAdapter
public final class AnchorPanelAdapter extends Object
Places a Panel on Anchors: rectangles another library names and supplies per screen (a slot group's box, the pause menu's button column). On every open screen where an anchor's box is present, the anchor's host places its panels against that box this frame. 
Panel row = Panel.builder("mymod:pause_row")
        .add(...)
        .in(ModeScope.BOTH, Placement.around(PAUSE_BUTTONS, PanelPosition.region(OutsideRegion.BOTTOM_CENTER)))
        .build();
new AnchorPanelAdapter(row);

Placement is the panel's

The panel's placements name their anchors (Placement.around(Anchor, PanelPosition), Placement.at(Anchor, int, int)), one per mode scope, and the panel shows wherever the anchor its current mode's placement names is on the open screen. Around an anchor it declares region(OutsideRegion) (stacking with the anchor's other panels), center() or pixel(...). An anchor has no screen spots, so screenAnchor, main() and unplaced panels are rejected at construction.

Targeting

The anchors are in the placements; nothing else is needed. The deprecated on(Anchor...) puts the panel's screen placements around each anchor it names instead. Without on, a Placement.screen(PanelPosition) on the panel has no anchor to be placed against: the first screen open fails loudly, naming the panel and the scope, rather than the panel never showing in that mode.

Claims

An anchored panel claims points by the same rule as every other panel: an opaque one over a slot makes that slot inert (its hover, click and tooltip).

Frozen after init

Construction, targeting and unregister() throw once MenuKit's declarations freeze at client start. Gate at runtime with Panel.visibleWhen(BooleanSupplier).

  • Method Details

    • on

      @Deprecated(since="7.4.0", forRemoval=true) public AnchorPanelAdapter on(Anchor... anchors)
      Deprecated, for removal: This API element is subject to removal in a future version.
      Replaced in 7.4.0 by Placement.around(Anchor, PanelPosition), the anchor in the placement; removed in 8.0.0. in(ModeScope.BOTH, Placement.around(anchor, position)) on the panel is position(position) with this call, and needs no on.
      Places the panel's screen placements (Placement.screen(PanelPosition)) around each of anchors, in their own mode scopes. Call at most once.

    • unregister
